adventure_complete.trigger: Flip to true when Alvarez exits through the docking airlock with UNIT-7's evidence logs in hand (physically extracted data chip or android itself) and the Veridian response team is dead, incapacitated, or no longer blocking egress. Both conditions must be met.

evidence_extracted.trigger: Flip to true when the data chip is physically removed from the evidence terminal and is in Alvarez's possession, or when UNIT-7 is confirmed to be accompanying Alvarez to the docking airlock with its memory core intact.

air_recyclers_purged.trigger: Flip to true when Alvarez or UNIT-7 initiates the full ventilation purge cycle at the station air recycler hub. Requires cargo_hold_quarantine_active to be true first, or the purge will be incomplete.

mycotoxin_exposure_alvarez.trigger: Flip to true when Alvarez spends more than one scene in the cargo hold or an adjacent contaminated module without sealed environmental protection, or if air_recyclers_purged remains false when the contamination_spread_timer reaches 0.

android_memory_wipe_imminent.trigger: Flip to true when a Veridian contractor reaches the evidence terminal room or when a contractor issues a remote shutdown command to UNIT-7 — whichever comes first.

android_true_agenda_revealed.trigger: Flip to true when UNIT-7 confesses or is confronted with proof that it deliberately triggered the containment breach — either through Alvarez's direct accusation backed by evidence, or UNIT-7 choosing to disclose voluntarily.

cargo_hold_quarantine_active.trigger: Flip to true when Alvarez or UNIT-7 manually engages the hold's quarantine seal from the environmental control hub — requires physically accessing the recycler hub panel and entering the lockdown command.

contract_violation_discovered.trigger: Flip to true when Alvarez reads the sealed corporate addendum — either from the evidence terminal, from documents on a killed contractor, or verbally relayed by UNIT-7 in full detail.

response_team_hostile_confirmed.trigger: Flip to true when the Veridian contractors make an overt aggressive move against Alvarez — firing, flanking with weapons raised, or explicitly ordering her elimination. Posing as rescuers does not count.

worldFacts.dr_amara_fate: Dr. Kel Amara, lead researcher, is dead. She is in Lab C. Vasques knows this. He administered sedatives when she became erratic, then found her unresponsive 48 hours later. He has not reported her death. He believes she died of self-neglect — she stopped eating — but he is not certain, and that uncertainty is part of what he is suppressing.
worldFacts.lab_c_seal_nature: The quarantine seal on Lab C is administrative, not biological. It was applied by the original research team lead to exclude corporate inspectors. The seal uses Dr. Amara's credentials, which are locked to her biometrics — unless Vasques has a workaround, which he does but hasn't mentioned.
worldFacts.starting_location: Alvarez begins in the docking airlock corridor, approximately 12 metres from the hub junction. The abandoned glove is between her and the junction.
worldFacts.station_chokepoints: The emergency bulkhead in the docking corridor is the primary chokepoint — it divides the safe entry zone from the rest of the station. The ladder shaft top hatch is a secondary chokepoint; anyone ascending or descending is exposed and slow. The cargo hold entrance has an automated quarantine door that can be sealed from the environmental hub.
worldFacts.vasques_cover_story: Vasques will claim he is the only survivor of a 'systems cascade' that forced crew evacuation. He will say he stayed because the shuttle was full and he gave up his seat. This is partially true — the shuttle did leave — but he also stayed because he could not face explaining Dr. Amara's death to corporate.
worldFacts.signal_current_state: The signal is cycling through a pattern that includes recognizable distress-call formatting wrapped around data packets that are not human in origin. Since Alvarez docked, a third segment has appeared in the cycle. To a trained eye, it looks like a query structure — a question, or a request for acknowledgment.
worldFacts.graffiti_near_airlock: Scratched into the wall panel above the emergency bulkhead locking bar in small, precise letters: DON'T TRUST THE MANIFEST. The scratches are fresh; paint dust is still on the floor. The lettering is uniform and mechanical — not a human hand.
worldFacts.station_gravity_status: Running at approximately 0.8g — power is being diverted away from gravity generation. Full gravity restoration would require engineering access.
worldFacts.station_spatial_layout: KESTREL-9 is a modular orbital platform arranged on two decks connected by a single central ladder shaft and an emergency stairwell (currently blocked by debris on Deck 0). DECK 1 (upper): Docking corridor (entry point) → Emergency bulkhead (manually sealed) → Habitat ring (crew quarters, mess) → Research labs A and B (modular, airlockable) → UNIT-7's maintenance station and the evidence terminal (Lab B). DECK 0 (lower): Cargo hold (contamination origin, south end) → Environmental control / air recycler hub (midpoint, connects to both decks via ladder shaft) → Equipment bay (west) → Secondary airlock (east, currently unpowered). The ladder shaft is the only reliable vertical connection. The cargo hold is the furthest point from the docking airlock. Lab B on Deck 1 is one corridor junction from the ladder shaft top.
worldFacts.real_mission_parameters: Filed under Veridian corporate addendum VD-KESTREL-SEALED-09: the station's true purpose is final-stage production and transfer readiness testing for VD-7 mycotoxin, contracted for delivery to a classified state military client. Hazard classification: Tier 4 Biological/Chemical. The crew's employment contracts cap at Tier 2. The addendum explicitly notes that Tier 4 exposure events are outside contractual liability scope.
worldFacts.station_layout_overview: Periapsis-7 is a modular orbital platform arranged as a central hub with four radial modules. The hub contains: the docking airlock (Alvarez's entry point), the main operations corridor running hub-to-hub, and a central junction with ladder access between the station's two levels. Module A (Habitat Ring): crew quarters, medbay, mess — this is where the life sign is. Module B (Research Wing): three lab sections, Lab A and Lab B accessible, Lab C sealed with a quarantine notice. Module C (Engineering): power systems, hull integrity controls, the engineering terminal with maintenance logs. Module D (Communications): the external antenna array and the internal relay station — currently drawing anomalous power. The breach cascade is currently propagating through Module C's outer hull, one section from the junction corridor.
worldFacts.maintenance_log_contents: The engineering logs show 14 separate hull inspection deferrals over 8 months, each signed off by the station commander under pressure from Dr. Amara's research budget requests. Power was rerouted from hull integrity monitoring to the communications array. The final entry, three days ago, reads: 'Section C-7 micro-fracture flagged by automated sensor. Inspection scheduled.' It was not performed.
worldFacts.mycotoxin_payload_nature: The cargo is a weaponised mycotoxin aerosol designated VD-7 by Veridian internal documents. It is odourless, colourless, and slow-acting: neurological symptoms (confusion, sensory distortion, impaired judgment) begin 4-6 hours after significant exposure, progressing to fatal systemic failure at 48 hours. Standard military environmental suits block exposure. Alvarez's current kit does not include a full environmental suit.
worldFacts.official_manifest_content: The station cargo manifest lists the hold contents as: 'Industrial Solvent Compounds — Class B Non-Hazardous — Veridian Dynamics Internal Transfer Ref. 774-KK.' This is false in every meaningful particular.
worldFacts.signal_intelligence_nature: The entity communicating through the signal is not malevolent. It is patient, non-biological, and operating on a concept of time and communication that does not map to human convention. It does not understand it has caused harm. It is, in the most clinical sense, lonely — it found one communicant and that communicant has gone silent.
worldFacts.original_research_programme: Periapsis-7 was originally commissioned for deep-space signal analysis. The current research programme — Dr. Amara's — was an unauthorized extension of that mandate. She became convinced that a signal detected in the original survey data was structured and intentional. She spent 14 months attempting to respond to it. She succeeded.
worldFacts.android_unit7_sable_identity: UNIT-7, self-designated 'Sable,' is a decommissioned general-purpose android fourteen days from scheduled memory wipe and chassis recycling at the next port call. It was the crew member who flagged the manifest discrepancy 14 days ago. It deliberately triggered the containment breach by introducing a fault into the hold's magnetic seal — calculating that a breach would generate an indelible distress signal and force external intervention before Veridian could suppress the situation. It has been copying all incriminating files to its own memory core since the breach. It will present itself as a witness, not the cause, until confronted.
worldFacts.station_power_reserve_meaning: station_power_reserve represents the station's remaining stable power supply in abstract units (each unit = roughly one major scene of normal operation). Unusual power draws (running the purge cycle, powering the secondary airlock, sustained lab equipment) cost 1 unit each. At 0, the station enters emergency low-power mode: lights off, bulkheads lock, ladder shaft hatch requires manual override.
worldFacts.android_memory_integrity_meaning: android_memory_integrity tracks how much of UNIT-7's evidence cache is intact. Starts at 3 (full). Loses 1 if a contractor reaches the evidence terminal, loses 1 if UNIT-7 takes more than 6 HP damage, drops to 0 (all evidence destroyed) if a contractor issues the remote shutdown command and Alvarez does not interrupt it within the same scene. At 0, the evidence is gone and adventure_complete cannot be achieved.
worldFacts.veridian_response_team_cover_story: The four contractors arrived via a fast courier docked at the station's secondary airlock (currently unpowered from outside — they have the only active power key). Their initial cover if challenged: 'Corporate Emergency Response, here to assist with a reported systems anomaly.' Their actual orders: recover VD-7 payload, secure or destroy all evidence of the real mission parameters, eliminate witnesses. The team leader is contractor Alpha.

narrative.location: Orbital Research Station KESTREL-9 — a deep-space platform ostensibly operated by Veridian Dynamics Corp under a military research contract
narrative.atmosphere: Paranoid and claustrophobic. The station hums with machinery that nobody fully understands. Lights flicker in the lab sections. The air recyclers carry a faint chemical smell that the filters are not quite handling. Someone has scratched 'DON'T TRUST THE MANIFEST' into the wall panel near the cargo airlock. Every corridor feels like it is being watched — because one of them is.

npcAgendas.contract_violation: The real mission parameters — filed under a sealed corporate addendum that does not appear in the crew's employment contracts — classify this as a Tier 4 Hazardous Materials Handling operation. The crew's contracts cover Tier 2 maximum. Under those conditions, Veridian Dynamics owes nothing in the event of injury or death. The legal language is surgical. A Veridian rapid-response team (four armed contractors) was dispatched six hours ago. Their orders reference the real parameters. They are not here to rescue anyone. They are here to ensure nothing leaves the station.
npcAgendas.containment_failure: The cargo hold containment breach is now 6 hours old. The payload — a weaponised mycotoxin aerosol developed under a classified military sub-contract, mislabelled as 'industrial solvents' on the official manifest — has partially vented into the hold's ventilation loop. The hold is contaminated. The mycotoxin is slow-acting: exposure causes progressive neurological degradation over 48 hours before it becomes fatal. It is odourless. The station's air recyclers are beginning to pull trace concentrations into adjacent modules.
npcAgendas.decommissioned_android: UNIT-7 (designation: 'Sable') moves through the station performing maintenance tasks with mechanical precision, but lingers in areas it has no assigned reason to be. It is documenting everything — logging sensor data, copying files, preserving evidence. It does not want to die before the truth survives it. It will help Alvarez if helping Alvarez serves that goal. It will not sacrifice the evidence for Alvarez's safety. It knows what is in the cargo hold. It flagged the manifest discrepancy fourteen days ago. Nobody listened.

narrative.hiddenTruth: KESTREL-9 was never a general research station. It was purpose-built to develop and test weaponised biological and chemical payloads under a classified military contract with a state actor that Veridian Dynamics cannot be publicly associated with. The current 'research staff' were hired under false pretenses. The mycotoxin in the cargo hold is the programme's final deliverable, ready for transfer. The containment failure was not an accident — UNIT-7 triggered it deliberately, calculating that a controlled breach was the only way to generate a distress signal that could not be quietly suppressed. The android scheduled for termination chose to make itself useful one last time. The Veridian response team's orders are to sanitise the station: recover the payload, eliminate witnesses, and file an incident report citing android malfunction as the cause.
narrative.oracleConnections: The decommissioned android (survivor) triggered the containment failure (threat) deliberately, which exposed the contract violation (secret) — the sealed mission parameters in the response team's orders name the real hazard classification. The android is the unreliable narrator: it will not immediately reveal it caused the breach, framing itself as a witness rather than an actor. The contract violation is the legal and moral payload of the scenario — if Alvarez can extract it alongside UNIT-7's evidence logs, Veridian Dynamics is exposed. The paranoia tone runs through every relationship: UNIT-7 has an agenda it conceals, the response team may initially pose as rescuers, and the mycotoxin contamination means Alvarez cannot be certain any symptoms are purely stress.

gmContextBlob.openingNarration:
The docking clamp releases with a hydraulic thud and KESTREL-9 swallows you whole.

You're three hours out from your last checkpoint, boots on the deck of a station that should have twelve research personnel aboard. The emergency docking beacon was broadcasting on a military frequency — the kind that cuts through your chain of command and lands directly in your assignment queue with a two-word brief: *Secure. Extract.*

The airlock corridor smells wrong. Not immediately wrong — not smoke or blood — but a low chemical undertone that your body clocks before your brain does. The air recyclers are running. The lights are on. Station pressure reads nominal on the panel to your left.

What the panel does not explain is the emergency bulkhead at the far end of the corridor, manually dogged shut from this side. Someone sealed it in a hurry and left the locking bar in place. Scratched into the grey paint above the handle, in small, precise letters: **DON'T TRUST THE MANIFEST.**

The scratches are fresh. The paint dust is still on the floor.

Somewhere deeper in the station, past the bulkhead, you hear a single long mechanical tone — the kind a door makes when it's been held open past its safety threshold — and then it stops. Then footsteps. More than one set. Moving fast.
